parameters.content:
## I.LPRB — LP report 133 "Jobs By Status" (thin transport ONLY)

Gmail → keep every **`.csv`** attachment → POST the CSV **text** → LP-MCP.
ZERO parsing here: every parse / validate / write rule lives in LP-MCP (fail-closed).
LP schedules this email ~6:15 ET daily · scope **cohort by contract date** · feeds Open backlog — HOA / Permit / Other.

**Eight triggers, one Code node.** The main trigger takes the daily arrival; the
seven month-specific ones (Jan–Jul) exist to pull historical months, since a
Gmail polling trigger is forward-only and cannot backfill on its own.

**⚠️ EVERY trigger needs `downloadAttachments: true` and the `attachment_`
prefix.** The January trigger was missing both until 2026-08-10: it returned
messages with NO binary, the Code node saw nothing to loop over, and it emitted
zero items — silently, because zero items is not an error. If a month never
lands, check this option first.

**Routing is by HEADER, not filename.** LP's CSV attachments are named
`_<YYMMDDHHMMSS>_Export.csv` and carry no report id, so the PDF-era `_133_` test
is gone. LP-MCP's `detectReportFromHeader` fingerprints the file; the slug in the
URL is only a hint. Scope comes from each trigger's Gmail subject query.

**The body is raw TEXT, not binary.** n8n's binary body mode sends multipart and
overrides Content-Type, which the route rejects with 400 "POST the CSV text as
the request body". The Code node decodes to `json.csv_text`; the HTTP node posts
it raw as `text/csv`.

**Node names still say "PDF".** Deliberate: `connections` reference nodes by name.
The wire is CSV.

**Failure handling.** 200 + `success:false` = deterministic rejection — never
retried; logged in `scorecard_ingest_log` + GroupMe. 5xx = transport error —
retried 3×, then reported to `/events/lp_report_ingest_failed`.

**Both outcomes now report.** The IF's FALSE branch goes to
`/events/lp_report_ingest_failed`; its TRUE branch goes to
`/events/lp_report_ingest_succeeded`. TRUE used to go nowhere, so report_type
`jobs_by_status` in `scorecard_ingest_log` could only ever receive failure rows —
which made 133 read as permanently broken for the eight days AFTER it was fixed.
